label: copy phase: first c of a doubled "c c" at original positions 2-3 (recall_idx 3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input is c (every activation has in_tok c, and it is never the first c in the sequence). In 92% of activations (94% of mass) the output is also c, so the original sequence has an adjacent "c c" pair: the model has just input the first c and must now output the second. Activation is concentrated where this pair sits at original positions 2-3 (recall_idx 3, 81% of mass), with some at positions 3-4 (recall_idx 4, 16%). It almost never fires for L=3-4. The largest examples are all "_ _ c c ..." with L>=6. It is very sparse and selective: only about 10% of copy steps where c is input and c is the output activate it, and about 40% at recall_idx 3, so precision tops out around 0.4. Other conditions I tried (digit count, the next output token, L>=6) did not separate active from inactive cases. Occasional weak activations come from c followed by a different token (c i, c t, c j). It does not fire in the original or delimiter phases, on any input other than c, or on a non-repeated c.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: c, i, t, v, j, a; least: o, p, h, -) and the current input token (most: c, -, 1, u, e, a; least: m, w, g, <DEL>); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=6 & t=9.
